change: the concept index reaches the practice hub from its quick nav instead of from anchor 52 of 52
_context: The last of the three cyber entry pages. The two course pages were fixed on
2026-09-04 and 06; this is the concept layer.
Measured on the served body 2026-09-06:
ap-cybersecurity-topics   52 anchors   practice hub at 52 of 52
and a second thing the measurement turned up that the board item did not
predict. The page has a quick-nav pill row directly under its hero, and that
row's ONE practice pill reads 'Practice' and points at
ap-cybersecurity-practice-questions. That page serves FIFTEEN questions,
verified independently on the live body: 15 data-qid cards, 60 options, and
the page states '15 question' itself, which is what board 197 reported.
So the single practice link a reader saw at the top of the concept index went
to the smallest practice surface on the site, while the hub that reaches every
quiz, lab, unit exam, the free response sets, the daily question and the five
unit spokes sat at the very bottom. Both halves are fixed here: a Practice Hub
pill goes into the row beside Course Hub, and the sampler pill is relabelled
Quick Sampler so the two are distinguishable.
NEITHER NEW LABEL STATES A COUNT. '15-Question Sampler' would be true today,
and is exactly the kind of hardcoded number that kept '40 MCQ + 3 FRQ' on a
live page for two days after the page stopped being that. The label describes
the shape and lets the page it links to state its own size.
THE GENERATOR GREW A SECOND MODE RATHER THAN A THIRD COPY. The band model
inserts a block before a unique anchor, which is wrong for a page that already
has a navigation row: the fix belongs IN the row, not in a second strip under
it. So a page may now declare `edits` instead, and the invariant is the
counterpart of the exact-split assertion: every `from` matches exactly once,
and undoing every substitution must reproduce the live body character for
character. Anything the edits did not declare survives that reversal as a
difference and throws.

THE ONE THAT SHIPPED THREE TIMES: make the guard existential instead of ordinal
checks._why: The first draft of the edits-mode guard asserted that the result LINKS the practice hub. That was already true of this page, from anchor 52 of 52, so the mutation written to break it could not go red and I nearly shipped a hollow check for the third time in one session. The guard is ordinal now, and this mutation is what proves it: relabel the sampler pill WITHOUT adding the hub pill, and the hub stays at the bottom while every existential check still passes.
checks.expect_failure: MUTATION: edits that relabel but leave the hub at the bottom are refused

checks.name: stop requiring each edit anchor to match exactly once
checks._why: An anchor that matches twice means the page moved under us and there is no way to know which occurrence was meant. Guessing is how an edit lands in the middle of something.
checks.expect_failure: MUTATION: an edit whose anchor matches twice is refused

checks.name: make buildEdited change something the edits did not declare
checks._why: This is the edits-mode counterpart of the exact-split assertion, and it is what makes this path as tight as the insertion path rather than a looser cousin. The first mutation written for it simply deleted the check, and the gate correctly refused: the suite computes the reversal itself, so deleting the generator's copy proved nothing. Reaching it takes a buildEdited that changes something undeclared, which is the defect the guard exists for.
